watching_for: I am looking for evidence of 'textual breakthroughs' for men—specifically whether 'dual utility' framing or high-specificity personal histories (like the DRC refugee example) can help men overcome the gender baseline.

specificity-accelerates-funding.title: High levels of detail and specificity in the pitch accelerate funding speed regardless of gender.
specificity-accelerates-funding.body: Pitches that provide specific lists of goods, family details, or current hardships fund faster than vague pitches.

family-dependency-slows-funding.title: Mentioning children or family dependencies slows funding speed regardless of gender.
family-dependency-slows-funding.body: Pitches that emphasize the number of children or personal family hardships tend to fund more slowly.

length-interaction-effect.title: Pitch length has opposite effects on funding speed based on borrower gender.
length-interaction-effect.body: Longer pitches tend to accelerate funding for women but slow down funding for men.

female-age-benefit.body: Including the borrower's age may specifically accelerate funding for women.

female-institutional-penalty.body: Mentioning specific loan amounts or institutions like NWTF may slow down funding for women.

male-dependency-penalty.title: Mentioning children's education or dependency may specifically slow down funding for men.
male-dependency-penalty.retrospective: Observation of similar penalty in women suggests a gender-general effect rather than a gender-specific one.
